target_customer: Mobile consumers who listen to podcasts (Podcast App) and adults with sleep problems (Rest, a CBT-I based program)
problem: Most podcast apps were built years earlier and are hard to use for discovery; separately, many people struggle with insomnia and want pill-free guidance.
business_model: Consumer mobile subscriptions and ads; Rest sells a sleep program with a free self-guided tier per its site
product_category: Consumer mobile apps: podcast player and AI sleep coach

founders.name: Martin Siniawski
founders.background_notes: YC page says nearly 20 years building and scaling consumer products with over 100 million downloads and hundreds of thousands of paying subscribers, both bootstrapped and VC-backed. Employers and education not named.

founders.name: Juan Ignacio Catalano
founders.background_notes: Listed as Founder/CTO in a search summary of the YC profile; the YC page fetch showed only Siniawski. Treat as unconfirmed.

competitors.name: Castro
competitors.traction_then: Shipped Castro 3 in 2018 with player rebuild and Apple Watch app

competitors.name: Overcast
competitors.what: Independent iOS podcast player with Smart Speed and patron-backed exclusive features
competitors.traction_then: Called the biggest third-party podcast app by a commenter; unverified

technical_complexity.rationale: Podcast indexing of tens of millions of episodes and recommendation playlists are standard engineering with some machine learning; sleep app adds content and AI coaching later.

defensibility.rationale: Podcast players are easy to copy and Apple bundles a free player; any edge comes from recommendations and download scale.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platform players pushed podcasts; third-party players were bought or shut over time (Pocket Casts sold in 2018, Castro sold in 2018), while Podcast App stayed independent and active.

market_need_then: Podcast listening was booming in 2018 and the TechCrunch launch coverage (2018-03-19) framed existing apps as years old in design with a 30 million episode library offered as a simpler way to listen.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct tagline: Stop scrolling, start listening

branding.brand_signature: Podcast App descriptive name with an App Store claim of being the most downloaded podcast app
branding.community_and_virality: Apple named Podcast App App of the Day in 2026 and featured it in Apps We Love, per the company about page.

brand_strength.rationale: A generic name is easy to remember but hard to search for and defend; recognition came from App Store featuring rather than a distinct identity.

pivots.to: Added Rest AI sleep coach as a second consumer product
pivots.why: not stated in sources; Rest app store listing appears around 2022

outcome_analysis: Evolve built Podcast App, which claims tens of millions of downloads, and later added the Rest sleep program. It raised small institutional backing from YC, Reach Capital, FJ Labs, Floodgate and FundersClub, with trackers showing a seed near 120 thousand dollars. No exit or shutdown was found and the YC page lists 23 people, so it looks like a lean, durable consumer app company whose growth rests on App Store distribution.
notes: Seed of about 0.12M dated 2018-03-19 appears only on CB Insights, Wellfound and PitchBook via search snippets, so unverified and not recorded as a round. A later July 2018 PitchBook deal has no amount. The company's about page lists investors without amounts. Catalano as CTO came only from a search summary; the opened YC page listed Siniawski alone. Competitor source dates are from search listings and the pages were not opened. Completeness pass: The seed round rests on a single database (CB Insights; Wellfound dates it January 2018). Investor lists differ between CB Insights and the company site, so only Y Combinator is recorded. The later July 2018 PitchBook deal has no amount and is not recorded.
